newsitem.title: CANADA: Canada spot gas prices turn lower after outage.
newsitem.headline: Canada spot gas prices turn lower after outage.

text.p: Canadian spot natural gas prices for September eased at Alberta delivery points on Wednesday after the end of an outage on NOVA's Knight compressor station in northwestern Alberta, marketers said.

The scheduled maintenance outage, on NOVA's Edson mainline, cut 1.2 billion cubic feet of gas transport for 36 hours late last week. A second-phase shutdown for in-line testing of the work ended on Tuesday.
Gas for September delivery at the AECO storage hub in Alberta was talked in the C$1.19/1.195 per gigajoule range, down from C$1.26 last week.
October gas was talked at C$1.17 per GJ, about the same as last week.
One Calgary-based trader said prices were expected to fall further on Thursday after players worked to get their accounts in order following the compressor work.
The trader said storage injections were also expected to resume in the second half of the week. Withdrawals at Alberta facilities were said to total 434 million cubic feet per day.

Meanwhile, British Columbia gas was trading stronger. Gas for export at Sumas, Washington was discussed at US$1.10/1.12 per million British thermal units, up a dime from last week. -- Reuters Calgary Bureau 403 531-1624
